productions.Label: Featured
productions.About:
Shakuntala is a love story from the Sanskrit classic *Abhijnana Sakunthala* written by the poet **Kalidasa**. The beautiful maiden Shakunthala who loves nature, treats all the flowers & animals with tender emotions and falls in love with King Dushyanta.

Romance as the primary emotion — presented as a musical entertainer with an engaging conversation between a bee and a bunch of flowers.
productions.Performers: Nirupama – Rajendra and Abhinava Dance Company

productions.Label: Featured
productions.About:
ABHIMANYU features the indomitable spirit of a warrior prince and the intelligence of the military in ancient India — the coding and decoding of different battle formations from the Great Indian Epic, *Mahabharatha*.

Highlights the heroism of 16-year-old Abhimanyu, son of Arjuna, who decodes Padmavyuha during the Kurukshetra war. Explored through Natyashastra syllables with shades of Kathak.

productions.Label: Featured
productions.About: A descriptive composition where verses are chosen from *Shri Krishnakaranamrutha* written by poet **Leelashuka**. The first verse shows the naughtiness of young Krishna; the second shows the separation of gopis and Krishna when he leaves Vrindavan.

productions.Label: Featured
productions.About:
Kalinga Nartana — a well-known theme from the childhood adventures of Sri Krishna. Krishna and his friends come to the river Yamuna; upon learning the wicked serpent Kalinga is in the river, Krishna climbs a tree and jumps deep into the water.

Agitated, Kalinga spreads his hoods while Krishna cleverly fights back, dancing joyously on the slippery hoods. The thousand hoods with glowing gems move in circles like a devotee's Neerajana offering to Krishna. Finally, Kalinga surrenders and people rejoice.

slots.value: We are storytellers hailing from the land of the oldest oral storytelling tradition — **Bharata (India)** — the Land of Cultural Heritage.
If you listen carefully, at the end you'll be someone else.
Based out of Bangalore, South India, our production house — **Abhinava Dance Company (ADC)** — stands as one of the premier dance companies in the country.
**ABHINAVA means "Classical and all-time-new"**, and as founders, our attempt is to create unique performances that reach out to a global audience.

cells.Text: Poetic performances weaving traditional tales, mythology and memoirs through dynamic movement and expression.
A rare blend of **Kathak** and **Bharathanatyam**, with vocabularies from the Natya tradition.
Stories conveyed through human emotions — light, sound, costume and ambiance creating theatrical spectacle.
Nirupama & Rajendra are one of India's foremost classical dancers — founders of Abhinava Dance Company, recognised worldwide for innovation, creativity, and imagination in Classical Art.
They are not only dancers, but also choreographers, teachers and storytellers with a vision of adapting traditional themes to reach audiences worldwide.
[Meet the founders →](about.html#meet-founders)

cells.Title: [Bharatanrityam](school.html#bharatanrityam)
cells.Text: Hailing from the ancient temples of South India, Bharatanrityam encompasses the ancient codified techniques of movement and storytelling that are described in the centuries-old Natya Shastra.

cells.Title: [Kathak](school.html#kathak)
cells.Text: With origins across North India, Kathak is a classical dance style characterized by powerful footwork, graceful spins, and expressive dramatic elements that are used in combination to tell a story.

cells.Title: [Natya Shastra Karanas](school.html#natya-shastra-karanas)
cells.Text: The Natya Shastra, also known as the Natya Veda, is a 5000-year old classical text on dramaturgy, wherein the classical dance styles of India have their origin. At Abhinava Arts Centre, students have the unique opportunity to explore the movement and theoretical content of this ancient text.

cells.Title: [Deshi Marga Adavus](school.html#dma)
cells.Text: A novel creation in the space of classical dance by Guru Smt. Nirupama Rajendra, the Deshi Marga Adavus (DMA) represent the bridging of Bharatanatyam's foundational vocabularies with the Margi Karanas of the Natya Shastra. [Learn more about DMA Research →](research.html)

cells.Title: Madanothsava
cells.Text: Madanothsava revives a 1,600-year-old community festival that welcomes the arrival of spring with the same rigour and vibrance once known in earlier times. Abhinava brings this bygone tradition into light once more.
cells.Text 2: The festival begins at 7 am as maestro musicians open the day with auspicious music. Artists then move in procession, wearing specially created turbans inspired by the Vijayanagara period. The festival is inaugurated with the release of Madana’s flower arrow — the God of Love — followed by song and dance dedicated to spring. Families take part in traditional games, and the community gathers to dance around mango trees.
cells.Text 3: From morning till night, the air fills with Indian classical vocals and instrumental concerts, sand art, various forms of classical dance, folk art, Sanskrit discussion forums and more. Through nature, art and culture, Madanothsava invites everyone to celebrate the gentle yet powerful advent of spring.

cells.Title: Yuva Abhinava
cells.Text: Yuva Abhinava is a unique initiative that empowers young people to develop skills in the allied arts — music, painting, literature and more. Talented and able youth are given opportunities to share their creativity with peers through intimate in-house studio concerts.
cells.Text 2: In these performances, the young artists introduce classical art to at least sixty to eighty new youngsters who have never before attended a classical programme. Through this simple yet meaningful exchange, Yuva Abhinava helps classical arts reach a new generation while nurturing the confidence and voice of emerging artists.

slots.value: Nirupama & Rajendra have dedicated four decades to preserving, innovating, and sharing India's classical dance heritage while creating new pathways for the future. From the very first production *Parampurush* (1995) to landmark research in Deshi Marga Adavu (2021) and national recognition with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (2023), Abhinava continues to set benchmarks in excellence, community impact, and artistic innovation.

We are storytellers hailing from the land of the oldest oral storytelling tradition — **Bharata (India)**. Our body of work is based on techniques derived from **Natyashastra** — a 5000-year-old classical text on dramaturgy. Over the years, our efforts to showcase the spectrum of Indian dance forms in all their grandeur has garnered admiration from over **7.5 million people** across the world.
If you listen carefully, at the end you'll be someone else.

slots.alt: Artistic Excellence — Abhinava production with fans

cells.Text: Rooted in tradition and creative in presentation, Abhinava’s productions are known for their magical storytelling, breathtaking choreography, original music, and exquisite costumes — all created in-house.
We have collaborated with distinguished music composers, master musicians, designers, and writers who have brought their creativity and artistry into the unique works of Abhinava.
This excellence has earned the **SNA Award** from the Honorable President of India, **Smt. Droupadi Murmu** (Category: Creativity & Experimental Dance), conferred at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi.
Over the years, Abhinava has built a team comprising choreographers, producers, creators, dancers, teachers, researchers and curators.

cells.Title: What is Deshi Marga Adavu?
cells.Text: Abhinava's Research Department has introduced **Deshi Marga Adavu (DMA)** — a new vocabulary of 108 artistically crafted movements created by Smt. Nirupama Rajendra. DMA bridges the Deshi Adavus of Bharatanatyam with the Marga elements from the Natyashastra. Know more at [Research (DMA)](research.html).

slots.alt: Nirupama and Rajendra — Artistic Directors' vision

cells.Text: To create a living tradition that honours the past while fearlessly embracing the future — through performance, education, research, and community celebration.

As founders of **Abhinava Dance Company** — one of India's most popular and cutting-edge production houses recognised worldwide — Nirupama & Rajendra have been instrumental in introducing innovation, creativity, enthusiasm and imagination to the realm of Classical Art.

They stand today as Artistic Directors with a vision of adapting traditional themes to classical media that will reach out to an audience that may or may not have context to traditional dance — with techniques from 5000-year-old scriptures to 21st century technological innovations.

slots.alt: Nirupama and Rajendra — founders of Abhinava Dance Company

cells.Text: **Nirupama & Rajendra** are one of India's foremost classical dancers, who hail from a family of educationists, artists and Harikatha Vidwans (traditional storytellers).

They are not only dancers, but also choreographers, teachers and storytellers. Their performances are based on Indian classical dance perfected over the years from learning in music, dance, literature and culture — some dating back to 5000-year-old scriptures.
**Family & Artistic Background:** Legacy of Harikatha vidwans from Purandara Dasa.
The audience has fuelled our passion for over 35 years and continue to inspire us to bring forth holistic and creative presentations for the world.

slots.value: The timeless way of learning dance, from teacher to student

Established in 1994, the internationally acclaimed training wing of the Abhinava Arts Centre offers a comprehensive education in Classical Dance. Recognized by the ICCR for excellence in preserving the Guru-Shishya Parampara method of training, our institution is a world-class facility where cultural education and traditional knowledge from legendary Gurus and Maestros are passed down with immense care. With students aged 5+ to 60+, the Abhinava Arts Centre conducts routine classes for students of all ages. No matter if you are a dance lover with a passion for learning, or a parent in search of holistic dance education, there is something for EVERYONE here at Abhinava.

cells.Text: Abhinava Dance School offers comprehensive training in Bharatanatyam and Kathak, rooted in the Natyashastra. Students master technique while learning to become polished performers, developing refined taste in classical music and literature.

The programme emphasises stage presence — dressing appropriately and carrying oneself with grace — alongside practical exposure to costumes, accessories, music, sound and lighting. Learners intern in productions, assist and lead rehearsals, and present work through both intimate in-house showcases and professional stage performances.

slots.value: Hailing from the ancient temples of South India, Bharatanrityam encompasses the ancient codified techniques of movement and storytelling that are described in the centuries-old Natya Shastra. The revival of this knowledge is credited to legendary Guru and scholar Padma Vibhushan Dr. Padma Subrahmanyam. Students at Abhinava Centre receive comprehensive education in Bharatanatyam, developing fine skill in the technical and storytelling elements of the Classical South Indian form. Learning at the Abhinava Arts Centre is further enriched by Bharatanrityam instruction. Abhinava Dance Company receives international acclaim for the unique presentation of Bharatanrityam — a 5000 year old movement vocabulary that continues to win hearts in today's age.

With origins across North India, Kathak is a classical dance style characterized by powerful footwork, graceful spins, and expressive dramatic elements that are used in combination to tell a story. At the Abhinava Arts Centre, students are exposed to a diverse and extremely rich Kathak parampara. Not only do Abhinava dancers learn the practical content of different gems within the Kathak tradition, but careful attention is given to a strong theoretical education. Abhinava Dance Company's Kathak repertoire is widely performed across India and internationally, receiving universal commendation for unique and innovative presentations of Kathak that remain true to the form.

The Natya Shastra, also known as the Natya Veda, is a 5000-year old classical text on dramaturgy, wherein the classical dance styles of India have their origin. This text is said to have been codified by the sage Bharata, and includes content on all aspects of performance: movement, stage design, practical content, even costuming. Within this text lies a unique movement vocabulary, known as the Karanas, that has been reconstructed and passed down by Dr. Padma Subrahmanyam. At Abhinava Arts Centre, students have the unparalleled opportunity to explore the movement and theoretical content of this ancient text.

cells.Text: A novel creation in the space of classical dance by Guru Smt. Nirupama Rajendra, the Deshi Marga Adavus (DMA) represent the bridging of Bharatanatyam's foundational vocabularies with the Margi Karanas of the Natya Shastra. The accompanying terminologies have been given in Sanskrit by Padma Bhushan Shatavadhani Dr. R. Ganesh. This vocabulary represents the excellence in both research and dance performance that are hallmarks of Abhinava Arts Centre.
[Learn more about DMA research →](research.html)

cells.Text: I must say, being at Abhinava Dance Company is an addiction. How immersed we get into the world of Art is magical. I have been learning Kathak here since 4 years now and I feel the difference already. Learning dance at ADC is more than just physical training. It's therapeutic. I consider myself blessed to have been able to closely witness the aura of Nirupama Ma'am and Rajendra Sir. I'm extremely grateful and proud of being an Abhinavite.

I was a part of this prestigious dance company as a kid for almost a decade and later had to discontinue due to board exams and so on. After 14 long years, I've joined back not only because they consider their students to be a part of everything but also because Nirupama Ma'am and Rajendra Sir have imbibed in each one of us the sense of discipline and passion towards dance and music. Thank you Ma'am and Sir for that. The fact that past and present students rave about this place speaks volumes of Abhinava.

Being associated with Abhinava Dance Company has been much more than just learning a classical dance form; it has been a deeply meaningful personal journey. In today's fast-paced world, many people may not fully understand the patience, discipline, dedication, and years of effort that go into learning a classical art form. Through Abhinava, I have learned that classical dance is not just about steps or performances, but about understanding tradition, expression, culture, and the stories behind every movement. The journey has had its challenges, but it has also taught me patience, perseverance, confidence, and a deeper respect for this beautiful art form. I am truly grateful to Abhinava for helping me grow not just as a dancer, but as a person, while keeping the true spirit of classical art alive.

cells.Text: **Empowering Young Minds Through Storytelling**

Class to Classics is a unique educational and cultural initiative by Abhinava Dance Company, envisioned to enrich young minds through the timeless wisdom, values, and narratives of Indian epics. cells.Text: **MADANOTHSAVA!** Revival of the bygone community festival to welcome the spring. A 1600-year-old tradition brought into light and celebrated with the same rigour and vibrance.
Brought into action by Abhinava Dance Company on **February 22nd, 2020** at Ramanjaneya Gudda, Bangalore — a brain-child of **Shatavadhaani Dr R Ganesh**.

The festival featured various artists for the whole day connecting with people: Indian Classical Vocals, Instrumental Compositions, Sand Art, various forms of Indian Classical dance, Folk Art, Sanskrit Discussion Forums and more.

Abhinava featured its new home productions: **Madananjali** and **Pramadvane**, inspired by the spring welcoming Madana. Apart from stunning costumes, props and extraordinary music composed by Sri **Praveen D Rao**, these featured new movements called **"Charchari"** — an innovation in itself.

slots.value: 108 movements · New vocabulary · Access on subscription

cells.Text: Abhinava's Research Department has introduced **Deshi Marga Adavu (DMA)** — a new vocabulary of 108 artistically crafted movements created by **Smt. Nirupama Rajendra**.

DMA beautifully bridges the *Deshi Adavus* of Bharatanatyam with the *Margi Karanas* from the Natyashastra (as reconstructed by **Dr. Padma Subrahmanyam**). These movements enrich pure *Nritta*, *Abhinaya*, and story-telling, offering infinite creative possibilities.

**Deshi Marga Adavus** are a new set of artistically designed movement vocabularies developed by Smt. Nirupama Rajendra — named in Sanskrit by **Shatavadhani Dr. R. Ganesh** based on their aesthetic and functional essence. Dr. Ganesh also guided the development process.
Pure dance — rhythmic footwork and body geometry enriched by 108 new adavus
Expression and storytelling — deeper interpretive vocabulary for classical narrative
The movement films are offered on subscription.

cells.Text: The movements draw on Nirupama Rajendra's training in music, dance, literature, and culture — from 5000-year-old scriptures to 21st-century innovations, within the lineage of **Dr. Padma Subrahmanyam's** Karana reconstruction.

cells.Name: Padmavibhushan Dr. Padma Subrahmanyam
cells.Small heading: 3 July 2019 · premiere of *Krishnaa — Fire to Frost*, Dayanand Sagar Auditorium
cells.Quote: “To bring the Mahabharata in dance is a Herculean task, which Nirupama and Rajendra have achieved. The concept was communicated beautifully and the choreography was unparalleled. I saw the true Bharata's Natya with all four abhinayas presented in an extraordinary manner.”
cells.Quote 2: “You should take this production to every nook and corner of the earth because you are reinforcing the greatness of culture and heritage values.”
cells.About: *Internationally reputed dancer and scholar, President of Nrithyodaya, Chennai. Recipient of the Padma Vibhushan, the Sangeet Natak Akademi's Akademi Ratna and the Fukuoka Asian Culture Prize.*

cells.Video picture description: Play video: Dr. Sudha Murty on Krishnaa — Fire to Frost
cells.Name: Dr. Sudha Murty
cells.Small heading: 5 July 2019 · special presentation of *Krishnaa — Fire to Frost*, Dayanand Sagar Auditorium
cells.Quote: “In general, women face a lot of challenges in their life but when we see the great difficulties faced by epic characters like Draupadi, it inspires us to deal with our troubles better. The saga of Draupadi was brought to life by Abhinava Dance Company in a grand manner even better than what I had imagined. The music, dance, costume, lighting, and the performance of the artistes touched my heart.”
cells.About: *Educator, author, philanthropist and former chairperson of the Infosys Foundation; nominated Member of Parliament in 2024.*

cells.Name: Dr. Veena Bannanje
cells.Small heading: 11 December 2021 · *Krishnaa — Fire to Frost*, organized by Bannanje Pratishthaana, Dayanand Sagar Auditorium, Bangalore
cells.Quote: “I, Veena Bannanje, the founder of the Bannanje Prathishtana, have organized Abhinava Dance Company's production twice, once in Bangalore and once in my village, Kalhalli. Witnessing this big scale production presented by the wonderful team was truly remarkable. Each artist brought profound and impactful artistry to the forefront, taking on multiple roles and characters from the epic.”
cells.Quote 2: “Innovative and remarkable, the technique employed to transport the Mahabharata era onto the modern stage is nothing short of mesmerizing. With each scene, the performance delves deep into the human experience, mirroring Draupadi's poignant life that tug at the heartstrings. It's an odyssey, a passage from earthly trials to celestial realms. Abhinava Dance Company's production Krishnaa — Fire to Frost is an experience that must be savored at least once in a lifetime. Nirupama Rajendra's portrayal of Draupadi's unwavering devotion, resilience, and elegance are brought to life with such vividness that it leaves an indelible mark on the soul. Their choreography, a symphony of movement and emotion, weaves seamlessly with the interplay of light and sound, creating a tapestry of enchantment that captivates the senses. To miss the production Krishnaa is to deny oneself an encounter with the sublime.”
cells.About: *Scholar, philosopher and orator with an enormous body of work in Kannada literature; recipient of the Kannada Sahitya Academy award.*

cells.Name: Shri Arjun Bharadwaj
cells.Quote: “It has been a great pleasure and privilege to have been associated with the Abhinava Dance Company for the last decade. I have been fortunate to have witnessed four times the staging of one of their most fabulous productions named Krishnaa — From Fire to Frost. The theme derives its inspiration from the grandest epic of India, the Mahabharata, and sketches the emotional landscape of Draupadi, the heroine of the epic. The choreographers, Smt. Nirupama Rajendra and Sri. T D Rajendra, have spatiotemporally recreated the episodes of the epic with such nuances that every movement is filled with suggestions and metaphors. The internationally renowned dancer duo are known for their exquisite choreographies which are rooted in traditional Indian theatre, but have a global appeal — their choreographies are a rare blend of the ancient and the modern, classical and the contemporary, material and the spiritual. The production Krishnaa aesthetically blends the grammar of many dance and drama forms of India. Watching the production not only entertains but also educates the audience on universal human values.”
cells.Quote 2: “I have written a detailed review of the first staging of the production in July 2019, published in a reputed journal, [Narthaki.com](https://narthaki.com/info/rev19/rev2388.html). Thereafter, I have watched the presentation three more times and I have always sought to watch it again and again. I am glad that the production has been invited for performances in the USA. My best wishes to the team.”
cells.About: *Author, researcher and translator with deep interest in classical literature, arts and philosophy; contributing editor of Prekshaa.*

cells.Name: Prof. Srinivasa Varakhedi
cells.Small heading: 27 July 2023 · organizer of the Yajnaseni conference, Kamani Auditorium, New Delhi
cells.Quote: “The uniqueness of Abhinava production creates an objective experience and leaves a long lasting impression in all viewers. It’s an enthralling and appealing play with multilayered effects to each and everyone. It touches one’s heart and reveals the inner Bhavan into many characters. Indian value system and cultures are reflected in these plays such a way the whole world will be transformed into a joyful theatre.”
cells.Quote 2: “I wish the team Abhinava all the best for their performance during US Trip 2024.”
cells.About: *Sanskrit scholar, academic and education administrator; Vice Chancellor of Central Sanskrit University, New Delhi.*
